title: WM multilingual fine-tuning — domain sensitivity gate
criterion: χ² test on active_dim distribution across language domains → p < 0.05

training.note: Flat VFE loss despite successful domain discrimination. ELBO KL and reconstruction terms adjusted in opposite directions, masking domain-specific h_t geometry changes.

memory_saturation.description: 128GB unified LPDDR5X nearly full (120/121GB) with Ollama 120B model + system processes. CUDA OOM during WM.to('cuda'). LR=5e-4 restart blocked.
memory_saturation.resolution: 30K steps at LR=5e-5 were sufficient for domain discrimination (p=1.47e-24). Future training can resume with --checkpoint-in and --device cpu or after Ollama unloads.

flat_vfe_loss.description: Loss 1.8058→1.8032 over 30K steps (Δ=0.0026). Domain discrimination was achieved through KL/reconstruction trade-off in ELBO, not through overall loss reduction.
flat_vfe_loss.implication: WM's h_t geometry changed to discriminate domains even when aggregate VFE was stable. This validates using argmax(|h_t|) as a domain probe rather than loss as a training signal.

triz_principle.name: Parameter Changes
triz_principle.application: Changed training distribution parameter (English-only → 8-domain multilingual) to break the degenerate English-only fixed-point attractor

next_steps.checkpoint_use: engine.py loads CHECKPOINT_ML if available (checkpoints/step_multilingual.pt). Generation now uses multilingual-fine-tuned WM.
